reason: Pure documentation task. The behaviour to document is fully visible in the repo: `mint release` tags the manifest version and requires a CHANGELOG entry but no intents (mint.mjs cmdRelease/gatherStatement; release.mjs ReleaseInput requires a non-empty changelog), `mint version` requires intents in .release/, `--no-push` exists (mint.mjs line 7/189), and the CI cut pushes the tag as github-actions[bot] via GITHUB_TOKEN (release-cut.yml ~line 325-332). No code changes, no credentials, no network beyond the clone needed. The ruleset-bypass claim from the issue cannot be reproduced in the sandbox (no GitHub org access), so it must be documented as stated in the issue plus GitHub's documented ruleset semantics.
current_state: README.md (/tmp/scout/mint-18/README.md) has a 'Use' section showing the steady-state flow (`mint plan` -> `mint version` -> `mint release`) and a 'Publish' section, but no 'First release'/bootstrap section and zero mentions of 'ruleset' or 'bypass' anywhere in README.md, docs/, or .release/README.md (grep confirms). /tmp/scout/mint-18/.release/README.md describes the intent format and the three commands only. /tmp/scout/mint-18/docs/npm-trusted-publishing.md covers only the npm entry-workflow convention. /tmp/scout/mint-18/mint.mjs: `mint release [--dry-run] [--no-push] [--no-attest]`; cmdRelease refuses if the tag exists or the tree is dirty, then `git tag` + `git push <remote> <tag>` unless --no-push; gatherStatement fails with a CLI message when CHANGELOG.md lacks an entry for the manifest version. /tmp/scout/mint-18/.github/workflows/release.yml is the single entry point: workflow_dispatch (dry-run defaults true, expect-version, recover-tag) chains release-cut.yml; push:tags v* covers a laptop cut. /tmp/scout/mint-18/.github/workflows/release-cut.yml guards: tag must not exist, .release/ must hold no unconsumed intents, `mint attest` must derive a statement; then pushes the tag as github-actions[bot] with GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write). So the two tag-creation actors are (a) the human running `mint release` from a checkout and (b) the GitHub Actions app identity for the dispatched CI cut; either must be a ruleset bypass actor if the org/repo ruleset restricts tag creation. The 0.7.0 CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md line ~25) notes 0.6.0 was 'manifest-only and never tagged', a real precedent for the bootstrap confusion.
plan: Add a '### First release' subsection to /tmp/scout/mint-18/README.md directly under 'Use' (after the `mint release` code block). State the invariant: `mint release` tags whatever version the manifest (package.json / jsr.json / deno.json) holds and requires a matching `## <version>` entry in CHANGELOG.md; it does NOT read .release/ intents (only `mint version` does). Then give the two bootstrap paths as numbered steps: Path A — set the initial version in the manifest by hand, write the first CHANGELOG.md entry (`## 0.1.0 — YYYY-MM-DD` with a body), commit, run `mint release --dry-run`, then `mint release`. Path B — add `.release/first.md` with `bump: minor`, run `mint version` (0.0.0 -> 0.1.0, prepends CHANGELOG, consumes the intent), commit, run `mint release`. Mention the CI alternative: merge, then dispatch release.yml with dry-run checked, then unchecked.

Add a '### Tag creation under rulesets (bypass actor)' subsection in /tmp/scout/mint-18/README.md immediately after the First-release section (or under 'Adopt mint's release in CI'). Document: a ruleset that restricts tag creation blocks `git push origin v0.1.0` even for org admins unless the pushing actor is listed as a bypass actor. Name the two actors precisely from the workflows: the human's account (laptop `mint release`, push: tags path) and the GitHub Actions app / github-actions[bot] via GITHUB_TOKEN (release.yml -> release-cut.yml dispatched cut). Instruct: before the first release, add the relevant actor(s) to the ruleset's bypass list (Org/Repo Settings -> Rules -> Rulesets -> the tag rule -> Bypass list), or scope the tag rule so `v*` is allowed for that actor. Give the failure signature (`remote rejected ... (protected tag / ruleset)`) and the workaround: `mint release --no-push` creates the tag and provenance locally so the tag can be pushed later by an authorised actor, or the dispatch path can be used once the Actions identity is a bypass actor.
Cross-link from /tmp/scout/mint-18/.release/README.md: add one line under the `mint release` bullet pointing at README.md#first-release so agents landing in .release/ find it.

Optionally add a one-line pointer in the header comment of /tmp/scout/mint-18/.github/workflows/release-cut.yml near the 'Cut and push the tag' step noting the ruleset bypass requirement for the Actions actor (comment-only change, no behaviour change).

Add a release intent /tmp/scout/mint-18/.release/docs-first-release.md with `bump: patch` and summary 'docs: first-release bootstrap + tag-creation bypass actor (#18)' per the repo's per-PR intent convention.
Run `npm test` to confirm the docs change breaks nothing (mint.test.mjs asserts workflow allow-lists, not README content).

risks: The ruleset behaviour ('fails even for an admin') is reported second-hand in the issue and cannot be reproduced in the sandbox; wording must attribute it to GitHub ruleset semantics (bypass list) rather than assert it was tested here.

Naming the wrong actor for the CI path: release-cut.yml pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN as github-actions[bot]; a ruleset bypass entry for that is the 'GitHub Actions' app / repository role, not a user — must be stated carefully or readers will add themselves and still fail on dispatch.
README.md is already ~12KB and dense; a bloated section could bury the two steps the verify criterion needs. Keep it short and numbered.
Repo CLAUDE.md requires claiming the issue via claim-ticket.yml before working; the sandbox has no GitHub credentials, so the executing agent must claim by hand or report the window as down.

The exact manifest bootstrap version (0.0.0 vs unset) matters for Path B: `mint version` computes from currentVersion, so the manifest must already hold a valid semver (e.g. 0.0.0) for the minor bump to yield 0.1.0.
